utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: While the witness is coming in, Mr. Cepic, can I ask you about one aspect in the statement. If you look, please, at paragraph 50 there's a reference there to Exhibit 5D383 just over halfway down. That exhibit has nothing to do with the civilian population, it's to do with exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour. It is the mistake -- actually, it has to be 5D838.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that one is understandable. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We shall alter the statement to reflect the Exhibit Number 5D838, paragraph 50. Good afternoon, Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your examination by Mr. Cepic will continue in a moment. Please -- sorry, by Mr. Ivetic, your cross-examination by Mr. Ivetic will continue in a moment. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you made at the outset continues to apply to your evidence today. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vukovic. I have spent the night trying to simplify a lot of my examination, and towards that end I would ask the assistance of the court usher to give you a copy of your statement, 5D1401 in Serbian so that you can follow along, and that way I can ask shorter questions and perhaps even finish sooner than I had anticipated. And when you receive your statement the first question I'll have to ask you deals with Cafa Prusit and I would direct you to paragraph 43 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If the usher can pass this statement, one copy of statement, to interpreters, please, it would be much more easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, what will happen is that it will be broadcast within the courtroom in e-court but not outwith the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, your --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just heard that interpreters requested the copy of statement, that was the reason why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, they have access to it if it's in e-court. Now, Mr. Ivetic, your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The question I have for you, sir, is: Here in the statement it says that the road was blocked in anti-armour sense and impassable. I would like you to explain what this means. Was the road mined or in some other way made impassable?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the road was not impassable only for armoured vehicles but for all types of vehicles, and any kind of civilian traffic as well. That is to say that at the Cafa Prusit crossing itself, there was an anti-armour minefield and anti-armour barriers made of concrete. The road itself from Cafa Prusit to the village of Zub was prepared for destruction, as we military men say. That is to say that mining wells were dug and a certain amount of explosives was placed in these wells depending on the type of destruction involved, from 50 to 150 kilogrammes. It was all linked up, so that would be about it as far as the road is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I take it then, sir, that the Cafa Prusit border crossing could only be undertaken on foot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No could not even cross that border crossing even on foot. I don't know from when, but I'm sure that from August 1998 it was closed even for border crossings within that immediate area. That is to say it was not operational. If you're asking me whether it could be crossed on foot, no, it could not because at the border itself, at the border crossing to the left and right of the road there were also minefields, here specifically mixed minefields, anti-armour and anti-personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did this situation remain the same for the entire duration of the war as far as the Cafa Prusit border crossing and the road leading to it is concerned?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, but I did not hear this right. Could the volume please be turned up a bit. I can't hear it right, and I can't hear the interpretation. Just a bit louder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, my question was --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's better now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question was: Did this situation remain the same for the entire duration of the war as far as the Cafa Prusit border crossing and the road leading to it is concerned?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the road is concerned, yes, but in order to enable civilians to cross on orders from our superior command we had to construct a passageway through the minefields so that the groups of civilians that, if I'm not mistaken, were on the move between the 28th of March and the 4th of April could go this way to the Republic of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that persons who travelled and wished to cross the border by vehicle would leave their vehicles at Zub before proceeding through this path that you prepared for their own safety?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those who insisted that they leave and go to Albania, precisely through this border crossing, had to leave their motor vehicles behind, tractors and whatever else they used to get there, because I've already said that we did not use that road, we the military, for our own traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'd like to move on to another topic, and to make that easier for you I would ask the usher's assistance to hand to you P1981, which is an order dated the 23rd of March, 1999, for destroying the STS in the wider region of Retimlje and for deblockade communications from the command of the 549th Motorised Brigade of the VJ. Now, sir, if you could take a moment to look at this document, and since you have it in front of you, you can actually leaf through the pages if need be, but I'd like to ask you if in fact this is -- if in fact the actions that you testified about in and around Celina and Orahovac that involved your -- Combat Group 2 and elements of the 23rd PJP, that joint action is a realization of this order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which paragraph of the statement are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It was the testimony relating to Bela Crkva, and one moment I can give you that paragraph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: From 27 onwards, but is there a particular one?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, there's not a particular paragraph but it's in that range. I'm saying whether that time-period and that joint action is, in fact, the one that this order outlines, that's the question I have.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've had a look at this. This is an order as in "zapovest," not order as in "naredjenje" to destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in the general sector of the village of Retimlje and to lift the blockade of a road. As far as I know, but I'll have a look once again, this order regulated this -- yes, exactly, the tasks of the units of the 549th Motorised Brigade that took part in this anti-terrorist action. If you're asking whether in addition to our unit a MUP unit took part as well, my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can perhaps direct your attention to item 5.5 in this order on page 3 of the Serbian and I believe it's also page 3 of the English, although I'm -- seem to have misplaced my English translation. Let me start with a simple question. Is this -- was the activity in Celina and Orahovac a realization of this "zapovest," order -- Bela Crkva, I apologise. I mentioned Orahovac. I meant to say "Bela Crkva."

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 5.5 that is precisely the task that is referred to, the assignment, given to my battalion, that is to say my unit. From a military point of view this is a classical way of issuing a task for anti-terrorist struggle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now just to -- well, I have a question I hadn't anticipated on, but I see the English translation is incorrect. So could you please read the first sentence of 5.5, sir, so that we could have the complete translation of the Serbian text.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "BG-2 of the 549th Motorised Brigade (consisting of: The command, the communications squad, the tank platoon, motorised company, platoon BVP, platoon PAT 30/2 platoon PAT 20/3, platoon MB 120-millimetres and the medical squad) in cooperation with the 4th Company of the PJP Djakovica."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, yesterday you mentioned that, in fact, the 23rd PJP Detachment had gone alongside your forces in this anti-terrorist action. Do you know if, in fact, the 23rd PJP Detachment is from outside the province of Kosovo and Metohija, from elsewhere in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic. Just a moment, Mr. Vukovic. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I think that this is not right, "set out together," I don't think that my colleague Mr. Ivetic stated it precisely the way it is stated in the statement. I think that his interpretation is somewhat different. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment. I have a response to that. I believe today at page 5, line 25, through 6, line 2, the witness testified that in addition to his unit a MUP unit took part as well, so if -- I'm talking about this same action, there's no confusion I don't think. I mean, if the witness is confused he could say so, but I'm just trying to find out whether in fact the PJP unit that yesterday he defined as the 23rd--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's a difference between acting along with you in some capacity and going along side with your forces. The English is translated. And it must have been the same in Serbian, so if you can put it in a vaguer way, I think there will be no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you identified the PJP Detachment in the Orahovac action as being the 23rd Detachment. Am I correct that the 23rd PJP Detachment comes from outside the province of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't have that information. I did not know what detachment came from where.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to this PJP detachment, the 23rd that you identified yesterday, am I correct that prior to this engagement in the Retimlje region, this detachment of the PJP had been in the municipality of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give a precise answer to that question, as I've said, but the knowledge I had then was that this 4th Company of the 23rd Detachment of the PJP was from the area of Djakovica. But as I've been saying, I did not have a document whereby I would establish that specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you did have this "zapovest," order, from your commanding officer, you did have that which identified them as the 4th Ceta, the PJP from 4th Ceta or squad I believe the English translation?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely what is written here, the 4th Company of the PJP of Djakovica. I know that on the decision map it said 4/23rd Detachment of the PJP, so I assume that that's the one, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. So on the map for this action all the -- all the PJP units involved and their locations and assignments were depicted. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, given this time distance, yes, they are depicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, now if I can direct you again to your written statement and paragraph 21 of the same, and I'll give you a moment to review it so you're familiar with its text, and then I'll ask you a question about it. And I think we could perhaps even finish with Bela Crkva shortly. The question I have for you, sir: Am I to understand from this paragraph that your head security commander was advancing together with the PJP or was he following right behind the advancing PJP?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that we're not looking at the same paragraph because in this paragraph I do not refer to any security commander, and I'm not saying that they went anywhere together. Perhaps there is some mistake involved, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... translation issue. Let me look at the Serbian. If I may revert to Serbian, this is notification for the translators --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please let -- if you want something retranslated, ask the witness to read it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could read for us, sir, the first sentence of paragraph 21 of your statement, that's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Upon exiting the village of Zrze by the silos, I waited for our unit from Prizren to pass and that is where I was contacted by the commander of the forward security and he verbally informed me that he had not searched the village of Bela Crkva because parts of the 23rd PJP Djakovica had already been in the village."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, with respect to the commander of the forward security, am I to understand that he was advancing together with the PJP or was following behind after the PJP had advanced through Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question. I just know that I gave him the assignment to go ahead of the bulk of Combat Group 2, that is what their purpose is according to the rules, to secure the unit on the march and in this case to ensure unhindered and safe passage as well as taking up the line of blockade. For this anti-terrorist action, it was to the east of the road between Zrze and Orahovac. If I'm provided with a map I can indicate that specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that's enough for that -- for our purposes right now. If anyone else needs a map I can have them call it up. I have one more question for you regarding Bela Crkva and two more questions relating to Celina. With respect to Bela Crkva, did you at any time while in Kosovo hear credible reports from any of your subordinates that either VJ or MUP units had killed 54 Kosovo Albanian civilians allegedly on the 25th of March, 1999, in the area of the railway bridge in the Bela Crkva sector?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I did not receive such information, but I repeat that I could receive information exclusively for my own unit not for the MUP unit. I heard of that alleged crime at a different trial here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And based on your knowledge and the reports that you received, you don't believe that occurred, do you, without somebody noticing?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the 25th of March, 1999, I am convinced that what at least was conveyed to me is something that did not happen because I was there personally in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, looking down at paragraph 24 of your statement it talks about going through Celina. Am I correct that before you personally passed through this village the PJP police and parts of the VJ had already passed through the village?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again it seems that we are not speaking about the same paragraph. As for the village of Celina I can answer you. From this village the first actions came against my unit and the MUP unit that morning. You asked if they had already passed through before I arrived, the police had searched the village, and before that the terrorists were neutralized in their entrenched houses and trenches. The police searched the village, they passed through the village, and a part of my unit passed through together with me, if I remember correctly, sometime around 10.00. That would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That suffices for me, sir. Now, if I could ask you my last question relating to Celina. When passing through the village did you see anyone, including elements of your forces or the police, burning houses, destroying mosques, or looting in the village?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, you will now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to talk about that exhibit that Mr. Ivetic was just showing you, which is Exhibit P1981, which includes a task for your Battle Group 2 in item 5.5 and the English translation I had said the task was to carry out an energetic attack and search the village of Bela Crkva. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the war diary or the war log for the 2nd Motorised Battalion you'll probably recall from your testimony in the Milosevic case that there is an entry in that document saying that's what happened, that Bela Crkva was blocked and cleared on that day; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the war diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as I recall your testimony in that case, you explained that even though that was written in the diary that was not accurate or correct. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said and explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And could you explain for these Judges here today why that entry in your war diary is not accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which paragraph of the statement should we be looking at, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not in the statement. I was referring to his testimony in Milosevic. I don't have a page citation but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I understand that, but this matter's not dealt with in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I don't believe so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the war diary is Exhibit P2019 and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's an entry for the 25th of March and I think 0130 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can assist, paragraph 23 of the statement does appear to address this. I don't know if that helps any, but it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thanks, I thought I had read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Oh, I stand corrected, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, it is there. So you want to formulate the question differently?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Colonel, it may assist if you could look at paragraph 23 of your statement, where there is a reference to that entry in your war diary. Now, you said at the end of the day you radioed your command post and provided the information about what had happened that day. What time of day did you pass this message on?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day the combat actions were completed at about 1800 hours, and then when I gathered all the formations it was probably around 1900 hours. But I'm really unable to give you an exact time. It was definitely not before 1800 hours and it was probably half an hour to an hour after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What was the name of your deputy who made that entry in the diary?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My deputy was captain first class Dragisa Milenkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, we've seen similar war diaries and combat reports where often there's a reference simply saying: The assigned task was completed. Is that a phrase that you might use when reporting about what you had done in connection with assigned task?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the most important activities are entered into the war diary, the most important activities of the unit for that day, the most important orders received, and there was such a term as well and it was in accordance with the order of the commander, strictly confidential such and such a number. So it is possible that such information was entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, in this particular case what did you say to your deputy, if you recall now?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that, of course. These were just brief communications for a number of reasons that I can talk about, but basically I just informed him about the axis where we were at the time, the unit, and from what I can remember, I told him that everything was proceeding according to plan precisely because that first day we didn't have any losses. It was just a short piece of information or exchange of information that took perhaps a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So do you know why he didn't simply write: Everything proceeded according to plan, and instead wrote specifically that: The village of Bela Crkva had been swept and blocked or blocked and swept?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My deputy at the basic command post had this "zapovest" of the brigade commander which Mr. Ivetic showed me a little bit earlier. He received information from me that we had reached a certain line, he had a map in front of him, he had the "zapovest" where the task was noted, and that entry that you are quoting from the war diary is something that he practically copied from the actual item 5.4 of the assignment; and I would say he did this automatically because at that point in time he didn't have any more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When did you first become aware that what he had written was not accurate or not consistent with what you tell us actually happened on that first day?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out about it in preparation for my previous testimony when the legal advisors of President Milosevic showed me that particular document and that's when I read it thoroughly. So this was in early 2005, but please don't hold me to that. It was definitely in 2005 sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You didn't notice or become aware of that in 2003 when you were giving statements to the VJ Commission For Cooperation with the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, at that time I did not have my war diary available. It was archived at the time from what I know -- actually, I don't know. I wasn't involved in the archive keeping, but it definitely was not accessible to me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as the commander is it ultimately your responsibility for the accuracy of the war diary or that somebody else's job?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From formal, legal aspect the commander of the unit is responsible for everything that is going on in the unit including this war diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. In your statement I think there's one typographical error in paragraph 2 it says you assumed your duty as commander of the 2nd Motorised Battalion on 4 August 1989. I assume that should be 1998? Maybe the English is wrong. I don't have the B/C/S in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: With your leave --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's evidently a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: There is an error in the statement in paragraph 2 because I just heard from my learned friend it is marked -- the year is 1999, it is not; it is 1998 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 16, Colonel, you mentioned being dispatched to a motorised company -- or dispatching a motorised company to Kramovik village to be included in Combat Group 4. And then in the second half of October 1998 that company was integrated by Combat Group 3 of the 549th until the war started. My question is: What group were you in command of? Were you in command of Battle Group 2 in 1998 or 1999 or both? I'm not clear on when it came into existence.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Battle Group 2 - and this is something you can find also in paragraph 6 - was formed on the basis of the "naredjenje," order, of the Chief of the General Staff on permanent measures of raised combat-readiness, and on the basis of that order, my command drafted its own order before I came to Djakovica to that battalion, in 1998 thus.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that -- that doesn't answer the question. The question was: Were you in command of Battle Group 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I was the commander of Combat Group 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what was the date from which you were the commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the 4th of August, 1998, when I assumed the -- my duties in that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you -- or did you also serve then as commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I was appointed commander of the battalion and Combat Group 2 was part of the battalion that was in the theatre so that the commander of the battalion was the commander of that combat group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I had difficulty with that when I was reading the statement. I don't think it's clear in the statement, but it may be I'm missing something. Please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I am too, Your Honour. Let me follow-up for my own purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not clear, Colonel, on the difference between Combat Group 2 and the 2nd Motorised Battalion. Is Combat Group 2 a smaller part of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. Combat Group 2 is a smaller part of the battalion strengthened with some formations from outside the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So all of the components of the battle group -- or Combat Group 2 don't necessarily come from the 2nd Battalion. Some of them come from some other battalion?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case they were not only from the 2nd Battalion, they were specifically also from the 552nd Artillery Rocket Brigade of the PVO, so there was a battery of anti-armour guns of 30-millimetre, and part of the rear platoon because in its peacetime composition the battalion did not have its own rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And when they are attached to that combat group then they fall under your personal command as opposed to their normal brigade commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's always like that. When resubordination -- when a unit is resubordinated, then in -- they are responsible or answer in every aspect to the commander of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And those components or individuals or subordinate units in your 2nd Motorised Battalion which were not part of the combat group, were they parts of any other combat group?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I really didn't understand what you are asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, if I understood correctly, some parts of your battalion were included within Battle Group 2, right so far?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. The remaining parts of your battalion, were they simply in the battalion or did some of them become parts of other battle groups, like the 1st or the 3rd through the 7th?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now it's clear. A part of the battalion was in the barracks the whole time performing its regular duties and assignments, training, security of the facilities, and so on, and I wrote here that one company from that battalion, the 2nd Battalion of mine, I sent to another combat group, Combat Group 4 to the Kramovik sector. I assume, since I didn't draft the order, that when there was no longer any need for that unit to be in that area; it was transferred to some other location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what happened to that company that went to Combat Group 4, did it ever come back to your battalion?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote here that it moved to Damjane from Kramovik to Combat Group 3, and then once the aggression began I received the order on the 3rd of April, 1999, if I remember correctly, and that unit or that company was again returned to my force. Or if you would rather that I put it in this way, from that point on it was again under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know if that assists Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us -- in paragraph 19 you tell us that your battle group consisted of 186 personnel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either I didn't understand you or there was a mistake. Paragraph 18 -- well, let me just take a look. That paragraph doesn't mention my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's paragraph 19.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that one either. It talks about this anti-terrorist action -- oh, excuse me, yes, but this number, 186 men refers to the execution of the task to destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the broader area of Retimlje, and then there is the blockade of the communications or the roads that go through that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We'll come to one of those orders later. Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How does this formation of Combat Group 2 fit in with the creation of Combat Group 2 in paragraph 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this doesn't really fit with what I know. My unit was the 2nd Motorised Battalion. Any specific assignment involving -- that I send a unit from my battalion, it would always bear the markings BG 549 MTBR, so that way you would know exactly which unit was involved. However, combat groups were temporarily forces that were formed for the execution of a specific task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I -- oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But Combat Group 2 referred to in paragraph 6 was formed with the object of providing in-depth security of the state border, which was a constant task in the circumstances that prevailed. Was it subsequently disbanded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That group existed until we started to organize the defence, but if we look carefully I assigned a certain number of forces from that group or units, as you say, and then the brigade commander sent some reinforcements to me. So then this newly formed combat group went to this area on this assignment according to this "zapovest" that was issued. Specifically for this assignment it was strengthened by a tank platoon which I did not have under my command previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So in March this combat group was reconstituted in light of the new task, and you told us that a tank platoon was added. One other difference I see it looks like a mechanised platoon was added to what you had listed in paragraph 6 when you were doing in-depth security. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid you didn't understand me. This Combat Group 2 that was set up as early as 1998 was not transformed into this new Combat Group 2, which is what you call it. I'm talking about the assignment, the specific mission that was to be carried out between the 25th and the 28th of March, 1999. It was only an element of Combat Group 2 that now became part of this newly established group, and there was another component that was dispatched at the time by the brigade command by way of a reinforcement. As for the mechanised platoon, I don't have any specific information about that but it was sometime in late March that they joined my unit, and I'm afraid I can't be more specific than that but it was another resubordinated unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, please read aloud paragraph 19, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The Siptar terrorist forces sealed off the Suva Reka-Orahovac road and the Orahovac-Malisevo-Pristina road. There was the danger that the Djakovica-Prizren road might be blocked as well. For that reason, on the 23rd of March, 1999, the brigade commander gave me the assignment of setting up Combat Group 2 in the following structure: Command, signals" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't understand it, Mr. Hannis, but I don't know that it matters very much. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the next paragraph of your statement, paragraph 20, you tell us you made a decision and for Battle Group 2 to begin its march for carrying out the task, and you mentioned that you assigned a reinforced rifle squad led by Lieutenant Radojevic to secure the movement. How many men were in the rifle squad, that reinforced rifle squad?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the establishment, a platoon would have comprised up to 20 men, 20 soldiers. I don't have my own order handy that I issued at the time. I probably dispatched a combat vehicle to reinforce that platoon because you use whatever a platoon has in order to reinforce a squad. That was the rule. About 20 men I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. From that answer I'm not clear. I understood a squad to be a smaller -- a smaller unit than a platoon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right. A squad is always smaller than a platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So about 20 men and if I understood correctly they were to go ahead of the main body of your Battle Group 2 to sort of reconnoitre and check the way before the rest of you went?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true to some extent, but checking the road was not the only thing they had to do. They were also checking for mines and obstacles although their principal task was to search the area to make sure there was no terrorist presence. We had reliable information at the time indicating that new operations groups had been set up at the time by the Siptar terrorist forces, the Poduvica [phoen] Pastrik operation zone specifically, and we knew that there were individual attacks being launched along that road, especially in the Zrze sector. So that was their principal assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And let me ask you this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you able to hear us okay?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I'm actually better able to hear you directly as opposed to listening to the interpretation through my headset.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let us know if you have a problem with --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can hear the Presiding Judge, I can hear you, but the earphones are not working properly for some reason -- oh, it's fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And then you tell us -- well, let me ask you this: Who passed through Bela Crkva first among the VJ personnel that were involved in this whole action? What unit or what individuals passed through Bela Crkva first that morning, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know and how. As for the army, my forward security passed through. That was their assignment. They were expected to be moving ahead of the mainstay of the combat group as far as the blockade line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you: What about General Delic or then-Colonel Delic, did he not go through the village before you did?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That morning General Delic and I met. He had just arrived from Prizren with some of his units. We met in the silo sector near Zrze village. It could have been about 4.00, perhaps half past 4.00 that morning. As far as I know, General Delic did not cross Bela Crkva at all. He didn't go through it. He continued to march on with those units from Prizren. He even took part of my unit as far as Brnjaca, and then he sent them on their way to Kosi Brod. I'm not sure about this. A map would be handy, actually. But as far as I know, General Delic on that particular morning was never in Bela Crkva village at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Maybe a map would be helpful for us. Let me show you P95, 095, and hopefully, Colonel, and here you can see most of the area that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on that, keep Bela Crkva near the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, what direction were you coming from? Were you coming from Zub; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I use the pen to indicate that on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, you may. You can mark on this map. Can you -- I don't know if it shows on there where you started out from, but can you show us where you started at about 1.00 or about 1.30 on that morning, what direction you travelled.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one can't really see the Zuba sector here, but this is the road to Djakovica, and I was moving along this main road over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And can you indicate to us where you waited at the silos and had contact with your security commander? Would you mark with a number 1 and draw a circle around it in its approximate location.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the silo is actually marked on the map so it's this circle over here. I'm not sure if the interpretation I am receiving is accurate. It's not a security officer or a chief of security. This was the commander of the forward security detail, so this may be a case of inaccurate interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's Lieutenant Radojevic? Is that who we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Radojevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you also said in paragraph 21 that you personally informed the brigade commander as he passed by with part of the unit towards Orahovac. Did that happen at that same location, by the silos, or is that some other location?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was right there that I had to wait up for those units from Prizren to pass by in order to go back to my own axis. I had to wait for them because it was more difficult to take that road that they were supposed to take and get as far as the blockade line. This is a military thing, nothing more, and that was where I met up with the brigade commander; and I told him about the situation that prevailed on the ground. Among other things, I also told him about Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Before we leave this map, then after that conversation with Colonel Delic, he went on ahead and took some of your people with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. As far as I remember -- I should go back to the original order and read it, but I think Combat Group 6 joined him on the way and some components from his command and then he took one of my platoons, no more than a single platoon, and they headed down this road. I might as well mark it for you: Brnjaca, it's right over here, and they went as far as the blockade line. May I just remind you that this person was actually a native of Kosovo and Metohija and he knew the area exceptionally well. It was night-time, so it was only logical that he should be the one to take those units to certain locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are you referring -- to whom are you referring there, the person that was the logical one to take those units?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the commander of my unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, you said -- it's translated here as: "May I just remind you that this person was actually a native of Kosovo and Metohija, and he knew the area exceptionally well. It was night-time, so it was only logical that he should be the one ..." Are you referring to Delic?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was referring to Colonel Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you put a number 2 above that second circle you drew on the map to the north-east of Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you draw a line between number 1 and number 2 to indicate the route that Delic travelled to get to where you spoke to him to number 2. Did he travel along that main road there?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we give this an IC number, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, you started to say something?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me -- and, yes, this is the main road. It's the main regional road between Djakovica and Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And later when you went through or past Bela Crkva, did you travel along that same road with the remaining parts of your combat group?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To some extent, yes. As far as as this -- to some extent, yes. As far as a junction where the road forks off to Bela Crkva, and then I passed through Bela Crkva with some of my forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we show you now Exhibit P93. This is an aerial -- actually, I think I have two aerial photographs, Colonel, of Bela Crkva --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Before we proceed, Your Honours, this would be IC175. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haider.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, next on the screen hopefully you'll see an aerial photograph of the Bela Crkva area, and maybe you can help us. I don't know if you'll recognise it or not. How many times were you in the vicinity of Bela Crkva? Was this is only time, on the 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took this road once in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's page 8 of this exhibit, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it has been a long time, and as far as I remember I took the road once in 1998; and as far as I remember, and I think the document says that somewhere, on or about the 1st of April, 1999. But this is the only road, or rather, the only time I was in Bela Crkva was on the 25th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You're translated as the 25th of April. I think you mean the 25th of March, right?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So on this exhibit -- do you recall seeing the mosque in Bela Crkva when you were there?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I passed through the village while it was still dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell from this map which road you would have travelled on in passing through the village, from this aerial photograph I mean?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be quite honest, I can hardly be certain that what I'm looking at is Bela Crkva. I'm hardly an expert when it comes to photographs taken from a plane. I know that as soon as we'd entered the village we'd crossed a bridge spanning a creek, and then just outside the village there is some sort of a slope. If you can hand me a topographic map I'm sure that I can point it out for you, but there is no way I can be positive that what I'm looking at in this photograph is actually Bela Crkva, and I'm not familiar with any of the features.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Does --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we're facing north in this photograph. If the photograph offered a broader view, perhaps I'd be able to help you more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't have a broader photograph ready to hand. The map that we were looking at before, would you be able to do anything on it or is it too small?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous map, yes, I think so. If you need another map that is larger, I actually happen to have one in my bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let's try with the one I have first and then we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we pull up P095 once more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is the same map we looked at earlier and you drew some markings on for me. We'll bring up a clean copy again. And would it help if we zoom in on Bela Crkva and enlarge it for you. We can go one more time if that's better.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you draw on this one the route you took in going through Bela Crkva, because it sounded like you may have travelled a different route than Delic did from what you were saying earlier.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid you got me wrong. There was this place where I entered Bela Crkva with a part of my unit, and the same place was used as a point of entry by Colonel Delic and I can mark that for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Please show us the route you took on your way through Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. That was on your way to the blockade line that you participated in?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The blockade line starts around here where my red line ends. This is a very good map and it's crystal clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And looking at this and recalling what you marked for Colonel Delic, it looks like in Bela Crkva you took a right turn, whereas he went straight on down the bigger road. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from this map can you recognise where the railroad line runs outside Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. It's actually marked on the map quite clearly. You can see the railroad on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you're aware that there is a stream that flows between Bela Crkva and, I don't know, down towards Rogovo that crosses the railway line? Were you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I see that stream. I think it's called Belaja. It goes towards Rogovo, or rather, as far as Beli Drim, that line over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what the distance is, for example, between the silos where you were waiting and Bela Crkva where you turned right to continue on your journey? That's a fairly short distance, isn't it, 2 kilometres or less?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the scale is for this map, but yes, roughly speaking, 2 kilometres or perhaps 3 but no more than 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All that land between Bela Crkva and then to the south and the south-west and the west/south-west, that's a very flat, level plain or valley, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's quite flat, as you say, a valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but in 1999 were those fields, farm fields in that area?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The locals were working their fields, that year as well. I think in this area mostly they were growing vegetables, but I'm really unable to say. This was sometime in March --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But -- thank you, Colonel. The point I'm trying to make is that you can see a long way in that area because it's flat and there are no tall buildings or forest or anything else in that area, right? You have an unobstructed view when looking from Bela Crkva in the -- to the south or the south-west or the west/south-west?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You do have an unobstructed view if the visibility is right and during day-time, of course. You need natural light.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, could you find a time to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, could we give that an IC number and take a break now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC176, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vukovic, we need a break at this point. Could you again leave the courtroom with the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll resume at five past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, approximately what time that morning did you pass through Bela Crkva, to the best of your memory?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to the best of my memory, I passed there between 5.00 and 5.30 because I remember that already by 6.00 I had informed my commander that the blockade line had been taken up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And approximately how many men and how many vehicles were in your group that passed through Bela Crkva that morning? I know you told us some of your guys had gone with Delic. How many were with you?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have precise information about that, perhaps about 40 men went that way. I know that the tank platoon went in that direction because in the village of Bela Crkva across the brook there is a bridge, and we were not sure whether it will be -- it would be able to carry the weight of a tank, say 120, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that doesn't mean anything to me, Mr. Hannis. I think you asked how many men and how many vehicles, and I don't know what the 120 relates to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, the first part of your last answer was: "About 40 men went that way ..." Do you mean 40 men in the tank platoon went to the direction Delic had gone down the main road?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you that I don't have specific information about that, precise information. I know that the tank platoon went on, but remember that three times four, there's only 12 people in that platoon, and perhaps three or four vehicles. I really cannot tell you anything more specific than that because that's not exactly what I was dealing with. A lot of the technical equipment went the way that I drew on the map a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me be clear about that. The tank platoon included how many tanks?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are three tanks in the tank platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did they go the way you went through Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the same road up until the intersection, then I turned right, Bela Crkva, and then they went on for perhaps a kilometre or two to the Brnjaca cellar. It's marked on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go -- could we have another version of P95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have to stay -- remain ignorant of how many men and vehicles were with Mr. Vukovic? You're content with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I was going to follow that too, but I wanted to do something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Colonel, how many -- approximately how many men went with you when you turned right and went on to the place where you took up the blockade line? Is that 120 approximately?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you approximately 120, but that is really an approximation. I cannot give you any accurate figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And which kind and how many vehicles went with you in that group of approximately 120?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the way it was. As for combat vehicles there were three 30-millimetre guns; two guns or three of 20 millimetres, those are mounted guns, mounted on vehicles; there were three combat vehicles of the infantry; and four or five motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So on this map again can you draw one more time for us where you and the 120 men and those vehicles you just described went -- show us how you went to Bela Crkva and where you went to where you took up the blockade line?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have we not had that, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we only had him going through --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but the blockade line was in the bottom right-hand corner of the rectangle as I understood it -- but okay, let him try again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that's where you stopped to take up the line, correct?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly there. Already from here all the units got out of their vehicles and went to their respective lines. The blockade line was exactly from the crossroads here and then it went this way via trig 440 along the road. I cannot see here Brod, approximately that's the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You've drawn three lines sort of running from the south/south-west to the north/north-east, and in paragraph 27 you told us that about 7.00 in the morning you started sweeping the terrain along this axis on the -- in the direction of Celina and Brestovac; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written in paragraph 27 and that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And how long did it take you to reach Celina?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look. To Celina it was roughly two hours because, as I have said, already at 7.30 fire was opened from Celina against my unit that was on the right flank and at the police unit. As far as I can remember, the terrorists from the broader area of Celina, or rather, it was around 8.30 or 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Before I mark this and leave this mark, if I understood you correctly, the tank platoon had continued on down the main road in the direction that General Delic or Colonel Delic and those with him had gone earlier; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, exactly. Later on, if you allow me to draw this, it's like Kosi Brod.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. Could you mark with a T where the tank platoon ended up along the blockade line.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the broader area here, of course, together with parts of the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And if you'll put a circle around that for me, we'll give this an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to put a circle around the letter T or something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we can give that an IC number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC177, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, you are aware from your prior testimony in Milosevic, are you not, that the allegation in this indictment is that dozens of Albanian civilians were killed in the vicinity of the junction of the stream that we talked about and the railroad track on that day, 25th of March. You know that's the allegation in this indictment, right?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that that's the allegation in this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know also that the allegation is that houses were damaged and the mosque was damaged in Bela Crkva on that day?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you're also aware that the victims of that killing included a number of children aged 10 and younger?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember all the individual details now, but I know that there was a reference to children who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you Exhibit P98. This is one that you saw before in the Milosevic trial with a different number, but this is actually two aerial photographs from different dates put side by side. The photo on the left half is purported to be Bela Crkva on the 11th of March, 1999. That white building in the middle is the mosque. And the photograph on the right-hand half is dated the 2nd of April, 1999. You probably heard in Milosevic that that photograph is actually turned 180 degrees to what it should be to line up with the one on the left. Do you recall being shown these photographs in Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were some other ones, but I can say that I do not recognise the village of Bela Crkva here at all. Do you perhaps have a wider photograph, so to speak, of the broader area? I really am not an expert in aerial images. What I can say is that it seems to me that this is not a photograph at all from that area, from that locality, or perhaps it's turned the wrong way. I don't know. As for this creek that you can see here -- I mean, I don't know. I cannot say whether this is the village of Bela Crkva or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If you can't help us, I'll move on to another one and show you Exhibit P1792 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I take it the heading on this, Mr. Hannis, "buildings intact" and "buildings damaged," is simply a heading and it's -- these are not labels of particular parts of the photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, that's just a general heading for the entire photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's very misleading the way the two have been put together. The one on the right is the wrong way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The bottom is at the top. It's no wonder that witnesses have difficulty with these.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and we tried to explain that on previous occasions in the trial when we showed it to witnesses that the one on the right should be rotated 180 degrees so that the bend in the river runs the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, it looks like there's buildings that exist on the right-hand side that are not on the left-hand side, so that's more confusion to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think that's something we'll save for submissions, but if I could show P1792.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You recognise that, don't you, Colonel? That's the mosque in Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot give you an answer because I don't know. I really don't know whether this is a mosque at all or whether it was a mosque and whether this building is in Bela Crkva at all. I've never seen anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I would tell you we have evidence in this case from other witnesses that that is the damaged mosque in Bela Crkva, a photograph taken after -- some date after you passed through. I'd like to show you one more time Exhibit P93 at page 8. In the centre or near-right centre do you see that white building there?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see several white buildings. Could you please be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you see the juncture of the road coming from the lower left-hand side of the photograph where it curves around and then joins the main road? Do you follow that?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see several of these junctures.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I would tell you witnesses identify -- more than one witness have identified this as an aerial photograph of Bela Crkva and that's the mosque, the white building, with those domes like we saw in the last photograph is the mosque. And isn't the road that you told us you turned and followed through Bela Crkva, doesn't it go right past the mosque?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you a few moments ago, sir, that on this photograph I cannot identify the village of Bela Crkva at all. Would you have a broader picture, so to speak, so that I could see the main roads? Then I could tell you whether this is the village of Bela Crkva at all or not. I never watched this from this vantage point. After all, when I passed through this village on the 25th, I practically passed along the outskirts of the village and it was night-time. So I could only see the first houses on the left and on the right. It's a typical village with narrow streets. As far as I can remember, it didn't look like this, at least not this part -- well, I don't know whether this photograph is in the direction of the north or not. You see, it doesn't really mean anything to me, so I cannot give you an answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you one more question about this. General or Colonel Delic, now General Delic, told us that this road that you see if you go along the left edge of the photograph about two-thirds of the way up, you see a road running from the edge of the photograph in a north-easterly direction, he described that as the main road and the road that he took when he went by or through Bela Crkva. Does that help you?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, not as far as I'm concerned. However, in all fairness I did say that he is far more familiar with the terrain. Perhaps he did recognise it, but I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll move on then. You mentioned that later in that morning you were -- were you personally in Celina?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I passed through the village of Celina approximately -- at approximately 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you not see the mosque in Celina that day?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I looked at the map, in the village of Celina there was a bell-tower in the village of Celina not a mosque. I don't know if I saw it or not. I looked during the preparation phase at the topographical map and there is no mosque in the map in the village of Celina. I leave the possibility that the mosque was built after 1990 when the last modifications were made to the topographic maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you Exhibit P2445. Celina was not a big village, was it? Do you have any idea of approximately how many houses were there or how many people lived there?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have an idea. It's probably a small village and it's practically joined to the Velika Krusa village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't have an idea how many inhabitants there were in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this photograph you see on the screen in front of you has been identified by other witnesses as the mosque in Celina in March of 1999. You didn't notice that building? It had to be the biggest, tallest building in that village, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot definitely say. At this point I really cannot say whether there was a mosque at all in the village and I don't recognise this photograph, it doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at another photograph of it, P1800, 1800. What you saw was a before photograph. This is an after photograph. Did you see anything like that in Celina the day you were there? That's what the mosque looked like later.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, what do you mean "after"? But I don't know, it doesn't mean anything to me. You're asking me if I saw any demolished or rubble during the war, yes, I did. I could say a lot about that. I have a lot of photographs too in case this Trial Chamber is interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm asking specifically about this rubble which has been identified as the remains of the mosque in Celina. Did you see this?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When is it alleged this happened, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have the witness testimony in front of me as to the specific date that this was alleged to have been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It may be in Dr. Riedlmayer's report. I think there's also witness testimony about the approximate date, but I don't have it to mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 30 of your statement, Colonel, you mention coming across -- and I take it this is still on the 25th of March - about 2.00 in the afternoon coming across a group of civilians, about 200 of them hiding in the Hoca river-bed. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that, but the name of the river is Hocanska Reka river.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where is that approximately where you came across these civilians?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's approximately to the east in relation to the Celina village, some 500 metres to one kilometre. If you give me a map I could draw that in for you precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I made a mistake a little bit concerning the distance. I cannot really be precise without a topographic map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me move on because I'm using up my time fast. You said you told them to stay there until the army passed and then go back to their villages. First of all, do you speak Albanian?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't speak Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I take it, were these Kosovo Albanian civilians that were hiding there?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were Siptars.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you have an interpreter that you were using to talk with them?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I had many soldiers in the unit who were from the area of Kosovo and Metohija and they spoke Albanian, also a lot of Albanians spoke the Serbian language. So if you're interested in the specific case I can tell you how I communicated with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, did you use one of your soldiers as an interpreter in speaking to this group of 200?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before moving on, you were asked there to locate the river-bed and you gave the name Hocanska rather than the Hoca, which is in your statement. And you said it's east of Celina. Now, east of Celina appears to be a village called Nogavac. Is this river-bed somewhere between the two or is it somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what I remember, a little bit farther away. If you give me a map this Hocanska river, that's the name of it, Hocanska Reka, but it's actually a brook that dries up occasionally. But for now what is important is that this brook made a large indentation or a drop in the land of some 10 to 15 metres in relation to the rest of the terrain. If -- perhaps if we bring back the map that I looked at earlier I can show that to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's P95. Now, if we can enlarge the bottom right part. Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I can see it and if you give me the pointer then I can show it. It's true that Bela Crkva, that writing, covers it up a little bit, but this is that brook or river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And can you show us where it goes as it passes through the writing "Bela Crkva massacre site" or have you marked the area where the refugee were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that you can see it here, but on the map that I have there is a topographical sign for a crevasse or -- and so as soon as you pass the village of Nogavac these civilians were here in that section --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's what you marked --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- although this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- with an oval in red; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no more questions about that. Should we give it an IC number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC178, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 30 then that after telling these people to wait until the army went past and return to their villages, that you know they later went to Celina because the fire group commander told you about that. Who was that fire group commander?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask the Trial Chamber that I not say his name in open session. He has a family in Kosovo and Metohija, and I would not want to jeopardize the safety of his family, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no objection if we go into private session just to hear the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, we shall take that in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Going on in your statement, in paragraph 32 you mention on -- at dawn, on the next day, the 26th of March, you got a report about a larger group of civilians, about 500, in the area of Sarap. You passed an order to the squad commander to direct that group towards Velika Krusa and Celina. Those were again Kosovar Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these were Kosovo -- Siptars because in this broader area there were Serbs only in Mala Hoca and in Orahovac. The other villages were mainly inhabited by Siptars. It's true that in the village of Mamusa there were Turks, but the population mainly consisted of Kosovo Siptars.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
